options.text: Player to the dealer's left goes first
The winner of the previous hand goes first. For the very first hand of the session, fall back to dealer's left
After dealing, whoever holds the highest single number card in their hand goes first
Draw one and skip your turn
Draw one, play it immediately if possible, otherwise skip
Draw until you get a playable card
No Stacking. Draw Twos and Wild Draw Fours take effect immediately
Stack +2 on +2 only (any colour)
Stack +2 on +2 and +4 on +4 (any colour, but within their own card type)
Cross-type stacking, allow any combination (chaos mode)
May only be played if you have no matching colour. Opponent may challenge — caught cheating draws 4, wrong challenge draws 6
No restriction, no challenge — play it whenever
Must play a card if you have one playable
You may choose to draw even when you can play
You draw the cards and lose your turn
You draw the cards and are able to still play your turn
No penalty
Draw 2 cards, but only if called out before the next player plays their card
Draw 2 cards, callable at any point
Points-based: the winner of each hand scores opponents' remaining cards. First to 500 points wins the game
Wins-based: ignore points entirely. Just track who wins each hand. First to 3 hand wins wins the game
No-Wild finish: you cannot win by playing any of the cards that can be played on colour as your last card

7-0 rule: playing a 7 swaps hands with a chosen player; playing a 0 rotates all hands in the direction of play. Edge case: if a 0 or 7 is played as your last card, the person who would claim the now-empty hand wins instead
Jump-in: if you hold a card identical in colour AND number to the top discard, you may play it out of turn. Play then continues from the player who jumped in
Double plays: if you have two of the same number in different colours, you can play them together. Yes, this gives you a god complex.

Slap on Six (a.k.a. Slappy Sixes/Slap Card): when a 6 is played, all players race to slap the discard pile; the last to slap draws 2 penalty cards. (Semi-official — appears in Uno Flash as "Slap Card")
Stacking Skip/Reverse: playing a Skip or Reverse on the same forces the next player to skip too
Skip n' Flip: when facing a Draw Two or Wild Draw Four, you may play a Skip card to pass the effect to the next player, or a Reverse card to bounce the effect back to the attacker
Mercy: if a player ever holds 25 or more cards, they are eliminated from the game
